candidates.title: Will Max Verstappen beat George Russell in the Qatar Grand Prix?
candidates.rules_primary: If Max Verstappen achieves a better finishing position than George Russell in the Grand Prix at the Qatar Grand Prix originally scheduled for November 29, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary:
Additional Clarifications:

This market compares the two named drivers’ finishing positions in the Grand Prix. Results are determined under FIA’s official final race classification. Apply the rules below in order. Stop at the first rule that decides the matchup.

Did either driver fail to participate? If either driver was never entered, formally withdrew before the race began, or was otherwise absent with no official FIA classification status, each market settles at its last fair market price. A driver who qualifies and then formally withdraws before the race falls under this rule, even if the other driver starts.
Was either driver disqualified (DSQ)? If only one driver was disqualified, the other driver wins, even if that driver did not start or did not finish. If both were disqualified, it’s a tie.
Did the FIA list either driver as Did Not Start (DNS)? If one driver was DNS and the other started, the starter wins, even if they retired on the first lap. A pit-lane start counts. If both were DNS, it’s a tie.
Did the FIA classify either driver as a finisher? If only one was classified as a finisher, that driver wins. If both were classified as finishers, the better official position wins (for example, 8th beats 9th). Identical positions tie.
Did both start but neither was classified as a finisher? The driver who completed more full laps wins. Equal lap counts tie.

Payouts. The winning driver’s market resolves Yes and the other driver’s market resolves No. A tie pays 50¢ per Yes or No contract on either driver.

If the race is disrupted. If it restarts, use the official final classification. If it ends early, use the FIA result at stoppage only if the FIA issues an official result and both drivers had an opportunity to establish a result. Otherwise, each market settles at its last fair market price. A postponed race stays open if rescheduled at the same circuit within 48 hours of the original start time. Cancellation, a circuit change, or a longer postponement settles each market at its last fair market price.
